definitions: The total energy contained within a thermodynamic system, excluding the kinetic energy of motion of the system as a whole and the potential energy of the system as a whole due to external fields.
The sum of all forms of energy in a system, including kinetic and potential energy of its molecules, but not the kinetic or potential energy of the system as a whole.
examples: The internal energy of the gas increased with temperature.
Work done on the system can change its internal energy.
Heat transfer affects the internal energy.
